title: Fit vocabulary inside each fold before adding word pairs
summary: Compare unigram Naive Bayes with one adjacent-word-pair change on the same stratified folds. Original generated template texts demonstrate the fitting workflow rather than real tweet quality.
environment: Recorded with Python 3.12.14 and its standard library only on Darwin arm64. This local CPU run is the recorded environment; other environments are not covered by this receipt.
steps: Download and run the script with Python 3.12.14. No packages, weights or account are needed for the fixture.
Compare unigrams with unigrams plus adjacent word pairs; train vocabulary and class counts inside each fold. Both models use fixed Laplace smoothing.

Inspect per-fold positive-class F1 and the printed false-positive/negative counts. Use the receipt’s error IDs to inspect those texts in the recorded input. Retain a worse result and explain whether template overlap limits interpretation.

Optional: --csv authorized-train.csv reads unique id,text,target rows. Empty texts and exact normalized duplicates are rejected; choose and document any grouping/deduplication policy first. Generated CSV mode is tested; competition tweets were not run.
limitations: Generated template texts are not competition tweets; no leaderboard submission or historical reproduction.
Repeated templates make fixture scores unsuitable for real NLP quality; near-duplicate, entity and temporal transfer are not established.
Aggregate is mean fold positive-class F1, not pooled F1 or a competition score. Exact normalized duplicates are rejected; no silent row removal.
Memory measures traced Python allocations, not process RSS.
split_definition: Five target-stratified folds with seed 17; exact normalized duplicate texts rejected; vocabulary and class counts fit training rows only.
metric: positive-class F1 (zero when denominator is zero)
